mainTopic: A white-hot knife and skewer (שחיטה and the שחין/מכוה question for צרעת), and using a knife of עבודה זרה
overview: שמואל rules that שחיטה with a white-hot knife is valid, because the sharp edge cuts before the heat can burn, and the cut opens so the hot sides of the blade don't touch. The גמרא then asks whether a wound from a white-hot skewer counts as a שחין (boil) or a מכוה (burn) for the laws of צרעת. This matters because a שחין and a מכוה do not join together to make the size of a נגע. ברייתות define each type and teach that when the two overlap, the later one cancels the earlier one. The real case is a person who already had half a גריס of שחין when the skewer added another half, so everything depends on whether the blow or the heat acts last. Two proofs are tried, from שמואל's knife and from a ברייתא about a skewer. Both are pushed off, because a sharp blade or a stab is different from a blunt blow. Finally, רבה בר אבוה rules that a knife of עבודה זרה may be used for שחיטה, which ruins the animal's value, but not for cutting meat, which improves it. רבא shows the test can flip in special cases. The גמרא then asks why the forbidden fat on the knife isn't reason enough, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Slaughtering with a white-hot knife is valid
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that שחיטה with a white-hot knife is כשרה, because the sharp blade cuts before the heat does damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of שמואל: If someone heated a knife until it was white hot and slaughtered with it, the slaughter is valid. The sharp edge cuts before the heat burns.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a ruling: a white-hot knife may be used for שחיטה, and the שחיטה is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the heat might burn the סימנים before the cut is finished, making the animal a טריפה first. שמואל answers that the sharp edge works faster than the heat, so the cutting comes first.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Shmuel said:
If one heated a knife until white hot and slaughtered with it,
his slaughter is valid,
because its sharpness comes before its white heat.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: שחיטה with a white-hot knife is valid because the cut happens before the heat can burn.

steps.title: But the hot sides of the blade touch the neck
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל: even if the edge cuts first, the hot sides of the blade should burn the neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are the sides of the knife!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on שמואל's reasoning by pointing to the sides of the blade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's reason only covers the edge. The flat sides of the knife are also white hot and seem to touch the flesh around the cut, so they might burn it and make the animal a טריפה.

phrases.english: But aren't there the sides?
phrases.notes: He means the flat sides of the hot knife, which seem to rub against the neck while cutting.

steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's reason that the sharpness comes before the heat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason covers only the edge. The hot sides of the blade should still burn the flesh.

steps.title: The cut opens up right away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the place of the cut spreads open at once, so the sides of the blade do not press on the flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: The place of the slaughter opens wide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל: once the neck is cut, the opening spreads apart, so the sides of the knife do not burn it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the sides of the blade stay pressed against the flesh. The answer is that the cut flesh pulls apart right away, leaving room around the blade, so שמואל's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: the place of the cut on the neck

steps.whatToRemember: A white-hot knife is fine for שחיטה: the edge cuts before the heat burns, and the cut opens so the sides don't touch.

phrases.english: The area of the slaughter opens wide.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual clarification: the cut opens, so there is no contact
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The hot sides of the blade press on the flesh and burn it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The cut opens at once, so the sides do not touch the flesh.

steps.title: A white-hot skewer wound: boil or burn?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: if someone is hit with a white-hot skewer, is the wound judged as a שחין or as a מכוה for צרעת?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: If someone heated a skewer until white hot and struck a person with it, is the wound judged as a boil or as a burn?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question, also about a white-hot metal tool, this time for the laws of צרעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A white-hot skewer does two things at once: it hits the skin and it burns it. A blow alone would make a שחין, and heat alone would make a מכוה. The question is which of the two decides what kind of wound this is.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was asked among the scholars
a boil, a sore from a blow or non-fire source

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse this with the first topic. We have moved from שחיטה to the laws of צרעת. What connects them is the same idea of a white-hot metal tool.

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
If one heated a skewer until white hot and struck with it,
is it judged as a boil
or is it judged as a burn?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question using the same idea as step 1, a white-hot metal tool
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a wound from a white-hot skewer counts as a שחין or a מכוה

steps.title: What difference does it make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between calling it a שחין or a מכוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the question matters. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before trying to settle the question, the גמרא wants to know if the answer changes any law. This step only asks. The answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: what practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: For what is the practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the question of step 4 matters
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical result of classing the wound as a שחין or a מכוה

steps.title: Boils and burns do not combine
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that שחין and מכוה follow the same rules, but the תורה lists them separately to teach that they do not join together to make the needed size.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: A boil and a burn become impure within one week, through two signs: white hair and spreading. Why did the verse list them separately? To teach that they do not join together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the difference matters because a שחין and a מכוה cannot be added together to reach the size of a נגע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both kinds of wound have the same signs and the same one week of quarantine. Still, the תורה gives them separate sections, which teaches that half a שחין plus half a מכוה do not make one full נגע. So we must know which kind the skewer wound is.

keyTerms.meaning: white hair, a sign of צרעת

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the skewer question really matters: if a person has a skewer wound next to a known burn or boil, whether they combine depends on how the skewer wound is classed.

phrases.english: For that which is taught in a ברייתא:
A boil and a burn become impure within one week,
through two signs:
with white hair and with spreading.
And why did the verse divide them?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:18–28, where שחין and מכוה get separate sections.

phrases.aramaic: לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵין מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה.
phrases.english: To say that they do not combine with each other.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שחין and מכוה do not combine to make the size of a נגע, so their classification matters.

steps.title: What counts as a boil
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא defines a שחין: a wound from wood, stone, pomace, the hot springs of טבריה, or anything not heated by fire, including lead fresh from the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught: Which is a boil and which is a burn? If he was hurt by wood, a stone, pomace, the hot springs of טבריה, or anything not heated by fire, which includes lead from its source, this is a boil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that gives the definitions behind the question. This part explains what a שחין is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is: anything whose heat or force does not come from fire makes a שחין. Even naturally hot things, like the springs of טבריה or hot lead from the ground, still count as שחין, since fire did not heat them.

keyTerms.meaning: pomace, crushed olive or grape waste that can get hot
the natural hot springs of טבריה
because of fire, heated by fire

phrases.english: And it is taught in a ברייתא:
Which is a boil and which is a burn?
If one was struck by wood, by a stone, by pomace,
by the hot springs of Tiberias,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְכׇל דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא מֵחֲמַת הָאוּר,
phrases.english: or by anything that did not come from the heat of fire,
which comes to include lead from its source,
phrases.notes: Lead fresh from the ground can be hot enough to burn, but fire did not heat it.

phrases.english: this is a boil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the definitions that the question of step 4 depends on
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wound from anything not heated by fire is a שחין.

steps.title: What counts as a burn
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a מכוה is a burn from a coal, hot ashes, boiling lime, boiling gypsum, or anything heated by fire, including water heated by fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: And which is a burn? If he was burned by a coal, by hot ashes, by boiling lime, by boiling gypsum, or by anything heated by fire, which includes water heated by fire, this is a burn.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by defining a מכוה: a burn from anything heated by fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the thing that touched the skin is not fire itself, like hot water, it counts as a מכוה if fire heated it. Now we see the problem with the skewer: fire heated it, so it seems like a מכוה, but it also strikes like an ordinary blow, which by itself makes a שחין.
steps.whatToRemember: שחין = wound from anything not heated by fire. מכוה = burn from anything heated by fire. The two don't combine, so the white-hot skewer question matters.

phrases.english: And which is a burn?
If one was burned by a coal, by hot ashes,
by boiling lime, by boiling gypsum,
or by anything that comes from the heat of fire,
which comes to include water heated by fire,
this is a burn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A burn from anything heated by fire, even hot water, is a מכוה.

steps.title: When a boil and a burn overlap, the later one cancels the earlier
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that when a שחין and a מכוה are on the same spot, whichever came later cancels the earlier one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא teaches: if there is a שחין and a מכוה on the same spot, and the שחין came first, the מכוה cancels the שחין. If the מכוה came first, the שחין cancels the מכוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a new rule: on the same spot, the later wound decides what kind of wound it is. This sets up the case the גמרא is about to describe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 taught that a שחין and a מכוה cannot join together to make the needed size. This ברייתא adds that when one comes on top of the other, the later one wins. So it matters a lot which effect of the hot skewer, the blow or the heat, came last.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancels, wipes out the status of
A boil-type wound and a burn-type wound, two types of skin wound for צרעת

steps.confusionAlert: Don't flip this around. The wound that came LATER is the one that wins and decides the status, not the one that came first.
steps.whyThisMatters: This 'later one wins' rule is what makes the question about the hot skewer matter. Everything turns on which effect came second.

phrases.english: And it is taught: a boil and a burn,
phrases.notes: He means both are on the same spot of skin.

phrases.english: if the boil came before the burn,
the burn cancels the boil;
and if the burn came before the boil,
the boil cancels the burn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a rule about overlapping wounds to the definitions given in steps 7 and 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a שחין and a מכוה are on the same spot, the later one cancels the earlier one and decides the status.

steps.title: The exact case: half a boil already there, then the skewer adds another half
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the real case: the person already had half a גריס of שחין, and the white-hot skewer made another half a גריס.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here, what is the case? The person already had half a גריס of שחין from before. Someone heated a skewer until it was white-hot and hit him with it, and another half a גריס came out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes the exact case behind the question from step 4. This also shows the practical difference that step 5 asked about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נגע needs the size of a full גריס. Two half-גריס wounds join only if they are the same type, either both שחין or both מכוה. So whether the skewer wound counts as שחין or מכוה decides if there is a full-size נגע.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?
Half the size of a split bean, which is half the minimum size of a נגע

phrases.english: And here, what is the case?
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the question about the white-hot skewer from step 4.

phrases.english: For example, where he had on him
half a split-bean of boil from before,
and someone heated a skewer white-hot and struck him with it,
and another half split-bean came out on him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the 'later wound wins' rule and the 'no joining' rule to describe the exact case of the skewer question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exact case makes the שחין-or-מכוה question matter?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The person already had half a גריס of שחין, and the hot skewer added another half a גריס. Whether the halves join depends on how the new wound is classified.

steps.title: Which acts first, the blow or the heat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sharpens the question. If the blow acts first and the heat cancels it, the wound is a מכוה and does not join. If the heat acts first and the blow cancels it, the wound is a שחין and it joins.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law? Does the blow come first, and then the heat comes and cancels the blow? Then it is a שחין and a מכוה, and they do not join. Or maybe the heat comes first, and then the blow comes and cancels the heat? Then it is a שחין and a שחין, and they join.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts the question in its sharpest form: inside the skewer's one hit, which effect happens first, the blow or the heat?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using the rule from step 9, the later effect wins. If the heat is last, the new half is a מכוה and cannot join the old שחין. If the blow is last, the new half is a שחין, and the two halves join into a full-size נגע.

keyTerms.meaning: The blow or impact, which on its own makes a שחין
The heat, which on its own makes a מכוה
They join together to make the needed size
Or perhaps, which brings in the second side of the question

phrases.english: What is the law? Does the blow come first, and then the heat comes
phrases.notes: Read it as 'What? Does the blow come first...'. The word חבטא belongs with קדים.

phrases.english: and cancels the blow,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָוֵה לֵיהּ שְׁחִין וּמִכְוָה, וְלָא מִצְטָרְפִין;
phrases.english: so it is a boil and a burn, and they do not join;
or perhaps the heat comes first,
and then the blow comes and cancels the heat,
so it is a boil and a boil, and they join?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'later wound wins' rule to the case just described and lays out both possible answers.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In a hit from a white-hot skewer, does the blow act before the heat, or the heat before the blow?

steps.title: Trying to prove from a white-hot knife that the blow comes first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings שמואל's rule: a שחיטה done with a white-hot knife is kosher, because the cutting happens before the heat. This seems to show that the blow comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי זירא said in the name of שמואל: if someone heated a knife white-hot and did שחיטה with it, the שחיטה is kosher, because the cut comes before the heat. So it seems the blow comes first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from a ruling of שמואל about שחיטה with a white-hot knife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל says the knife's cut happens before its heat can burn the animal. If the physical action of a hot tool always comes before the heat, then the skewer's blow also comes first. The heat would then come last and win, making the skewer wound a מכוה.

keyTerms.meaning: White heat, the state of being heated until white-hot
So it seems, which brings out the conclusion of a proof

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rabbi Zeira said that Shmuel said:
If one heated a knife white-hot and slaughtered with it,
his slaughter is valid,
because its sharpness comes before its white heat.
So it seems the blow comes first!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the question in step 11 using a ruling about שחיטה.
steps.raayaObject: That the blow (חבטא) of a hot tool acts before its heat (הבלא).
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's rule that שחיטה with a white-hot knife is kosher, because the cut comes before the heat.

steps.title: A sharp blade is different from a blunt blow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. A sharp blade is different, so it tells us nothing about a blunt skewer's blow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from the knife: a sharp edge cuts right away, so it is not like a blunt blow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blade's sharpness works the moment it touches, so it can beat the heat. A blunt skewer's blow does not cut that fast, so the heat may act first. The question is still not settled, and the next step tries another proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Sharpness, the cutting edge of a blade
Is different, so the case cannot be compared

steps.whatToRemember: The question is still open: in a blow from a white-hot skewer, we do not know if the blow or the heat acts first. So we do not know if the wound is a שחין that joins with the old half, or a מכוה that does not join. שמואל's knife does not settle it, because a sharp blade is different.

phrases.english: Sharpness is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from שמואל's knife ruling.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not decide the question either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof compares a sharp blade, which cuts right away, to a blunt skewer's blow, which may act more slowly than the heat.

steps.title: A proof from a skewer that makes a burn mark
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a mark from a white-hot skewer counts as a מכוה. This seems to show that the blow comes first and the heat comes after.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If someone heated a skewer until it was white-hot and hit a person with it, the mark is judged as a burn from fire. So it seems the blow comes first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries again to answer the open question: in a white-hot tool, does the blow act first or the heat?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wound is judged as a מכוה, then the heat must be what counts. Whatever comes later cancels what came before, so the heat must have come after the blow. So the blow comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: a burn caused by fire, a type of צרעת mark

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get mixed up: the wound being called a 'burn' is what proves the BLOW came first. Whatever comes later wins, and here the heat won.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: לִיבֵּן שַׁפּוּד וְהִכָּה בּוֹ –
phrases.english: Come and hear: if one heated a skewer white-hot and struck with it,
it is judged as a burn from fire;
apparently, the blow comes first!
phrases.notes: Since the later effect cancels the earlier one, a 'burn' ruling means the heat came second.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from שמואל was rejected, the גמרא tries a new proof for the same question.
steps.raayaObject: That in a white-hot tool, the blow acts before the heat.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a white-hot skewer's mark is judged as a מכוה.

steps.title: The skewer stabbed, like a sharp blade
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. That ברייתא is about a skewer that pierced the skin, which is like cutting with a sharp blade.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, it is a case where he stabbed with it, which is the same as a sharp edge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from the skewer, using the same answer it gave to שמואל's knife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stab pierces at once, the way a sharp knife cuts, so of course the wound comes before the heat. That tells us nothing about a blunt blow, which is the case we are really asking about. The question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: he stabbed or pierced with it

phrases.english: There too, it is where he stabbed with it,
which is the same as a sharp edge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely. The question of blow versus heat remains unresolved.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's skewer stabbed, which acts like a sharp blade, so it can't teach about a blunt blow.
steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs (שמואל's knife and the skewer) are about sharp cutting. So the question of whether a blunt blow or the heat comes first stays unanswered.

steps.title: A knife of idol worship: slaughter yes, cutting meat no
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה rules that a knife of עבודה זרה may be used for שחיטה but not for cutting meat. Slaughtering ruins value, and cutting meat adds value.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: With a knife of idol worship, it is permitted to slaughter, but forbidden to cut meat. Slaughtering is allowed because it is ruining. Cutting meat is forbidden because it is improving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about a knife used for עבודה זרה and when you may use it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You may not get benefit from things of עבודה זרה. A living animal is worth more than a slaughtered one, so slaughtering with the knife gives you no benefit. Cutting meat makes it easier to use, so that is benefit and it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: a knife used for idol worship, forbidden for benefit

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
A knife of idol worship:
it is permitted to slaughter with it,
but forbidden to cut meat with it.
Permitted to slaughter with it – because he is ruining,
phrases.notes: A live animal is worth more than a slaughtered one, so slaughtering lowers its value.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָסוּר לַחְתּוֹךְ בָּהּ בָּשָׂר – מְתַקֵּן הוּא.
phrases.english: and forbidden to cut meat with it – because he is improving.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic about knives and שחיטה, after the blow-versus-heat discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A knife of עבודה זרה may be used for שחיטה, since that ruins the animal's value, but not for cutting meat, since that improves it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that forbidden benefit is measured by whether the act actually helps you, not by the act itself.

steps.title: Sometimes it works the other way
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds that sometimes slaughtering is forbidden, like with a dying animal. Sometimes cutting is allowed, like with thighs meant as a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Sometimes the slaughterer is forbidden, like with an animal in danger of dying. And sometimes the one who cuts is permitted, like with thighs that are set aside as a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds to the rule: what matters is whether the act really improves or ruins in this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an animal is about to die, slaughtering it saves it from becoming a נבילה, so it improves the value and is forbidden. If whole thighs are meant as a gift, cutting them up lowers their value, so cutting is ruining and allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: an animal in danger of dying
here: a gift for an important person

phrases.english: Rava said: There are times when the one who slaughters is forbidden –
with an animal about to die,
phrases.notes: If it dies on its own it becomes a נבילה, so slaughtering it now saves its value.

phrases.english: and the one who cuts is permitted –
with thighs that are set aside as a gift.
phrases.notes: Here קורבנא doesn't mean a Temple offering. It's a gift for an important person, and that has to stay whole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the rule of step 16 by showing that the test is ruining versus improving, not slaughter versus cutting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The real test is whether the act ruins or improves in the specific case. A dying animal may not be slaughtered with the knife, and gift thighs may be cut with it.
steps.whatToRemember: With a knife of עבודה זרה, ask one question: does this use help me or hurt the item's value? If it helps, it's forbidden.

steps.title: Why not forbid it because of forbidden fat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why do we need the reason of forbidden benefit? The knife should be a problem anyway, because forbidden fat is stuck on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him get the rule from the forbidden fat residue on the knife!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reasoning of רבה בר אבוה. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A knife used for idol worship has surely cut forbidden meat, so forbidden fat is stuck on it. That alone should make cutting meat with it a problem, even without the rule about benefit. So why explain it with ruining and improving?

keyTerms.meaning: let him derive it instead from

phrases.english: But let him derive it
because of the forbidden fat residue!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasoning of רבה בר אבוה that the knife's problem is forbidden benefit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Forbidden fat on the knife should already forbid it, so the benefit reasoning seems unnecessary or incomplete.
